bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the HVAC Technician Salary

If you're an HVAC technician in Australia, your pay is likely covered by the **Business Equipment Award** (MA000021). This award sets minimum hourly rates, allowances, penalty rates, and overtime for technical services employees. To work out your annual salary, you can convert your hourly rate using the standard formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. Most full-time roles assume 38 hours per week, which is the ordinary hours under the award.

For example, a **Technician level 3** (a common classification for qualified HVAC technicians) has a minimum hourly rate of **$27.96** for full-time employees. Multiply that by 38 hours and 52 weeks, and you get an annual gross salary of **$55,236.96**. If you're casual, your rate includes a 25% loading, so the hourly rate becomes **$34.95**, and the annual equivalent would be **$69,061.20** (though casuals don't accrue paid leave).

### How to Convert Hourly to Annual

Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to quickly see your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly pay. The formula is simple:

- **Annual gross** = hourly rate × hours per week × 52
- **Fortnightly** = weekly pay × 2 (weekly pay = hourly rate × hours per week)

For a Technician level 3 on $27.96 per hour, 38 hours per week:
- Weekly pay = $27.96 × 38 = **$1,062.48**
- Fortnightly pay = $1,062.48 × 2 = **$2,124.96**
- Annual gross = $1,062.48 × 52 = **$55,236.96**

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more personalised estimate, check the [reference tables](/data) for your specific award classification.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** (or $33.05 per hour for casuals). However, most HVAC technicians are covered by the Business Equipment Award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, a Technician level 3 earns $27.96 per hour, while a Technician level 5 (more experienced) earns $31.28 per hour. You can find the full classification structure in the [pay guides](/blog) section.

If you're a casual HVAC technician, your base rate already includes the 25% casual loading. When using our [the timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **superannuation guarantee** at **12%** of your ordinary earnings (for 2026–27). This is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For a full-time HVAC technician earning $55,236.96 per year, the super contribution would be **$6,628.44** per year, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830**. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross salary is subject to **Australian resident tax** and the **Medicare levy**. For the 2026–27 financial year, the tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 + 45% of excess over $190,000

The **Medicare levy** is generally **2%** of your taxable income. For a salary of $55,236.96, the estimated tax is approximately **$8,167** (including Medicare). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator to see your after-tax amount.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a Technician level 3, your fortnightly gross pay would be **$2,124.96**. After tax and Medicare, you might take home around **$1,800** (depending on your circumstances). This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Casual Loading and Penalty Rates

If you work as a casual HVAC technician, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The award also specifies penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, and overtime. For example, Saturday ordinary time for a Technician level 3 is $41.94 per hour (full-time) or $52.43 per hour (casual). These rates are higher than the base rate. Check the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for more details.

### Using the Fair Work Data

The rates in this article come from the **Fair Work Ombudsman** Pay Guide for the Business Equipment Award and the **Fair Work Commission** Modern Awards Pay Database. These are the official sources for minimum wages and conditions. Always refer to the award for your exact classification, as individual circumstances may vary.

### Summary

To estimate your HVAC technician salary:
1. Find your classification in the Business Equipment Award.
2. Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks.
3. Add 12% super on top.
4. Deduct tax and Medicare levy to estimate take-home pay.

Use our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide to compare different roles and industries. Remember, the figures here are estimates and should not replace professional advice.
